modules.title: The Georgian Alphabet
modules.subtitle: 33 letters, one sound each
modules.intro: Mkhedruli has 33 letters and no capitals. Each letter has one sound, so once you know them you can read any word aloud.

lessons.title: Tight or with air?
lessons.note: Five sounds come in pairs: one tight, with no air (კ პ ტ წ ჭ), and one with a puff of air, like English (ქ ფ თ ც ჩ). They make different words: კარი is a door, ქარი is the wind.

notes.title: Personal pronouns
notes.text: Georgian has six. There is no he or she: ის means he, she and it.

exercises.explanation: ჩვენ is we; თქვენ is you (plural or polite).
Georgian doesn't mark he or she.

exercises.prompt: Talking politely to an older stranger, "you" is…
exercises.explanation: თქვენ is the polite you, even for one person.
ვართ is "we are", so the pronoun is ჩვენ.

notes.title: I am, you are
notes.text: The verb "to be" changes with the person. It usually comes at the end of the sentence.

notes.title: The short -ა
notes.text: არის is often shortened to -ა at the end of the word before it.

exercises.explanation: -ა at the end is short for არის.

notes.title: The present tense
notes.text: The start and end of a verb show who is doing it: ვ- for I and we, -ს for he or she, -თ for plural, -ენ for they.

notes.title: Word order
notes.text: The verb usually comes last: მე ქართულს ვსწავლობ, "I Georgian learn". Other orders are fine too.

exercises.prompt: In ის წერს, which part means "he / she"?

lessons.title: Want, love, have

notes.title: Verbs that work the other way
notes.text: Some everyday verbs put "me" inside the verb with მ-, and "you" with გ-. The thing you want or have stays in its plain form.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "I want coffee"?

lessons.subtitle: Verbs that work the other way

notes.title: Question words
notes.text: The question word usually comes just before the verb.

notes.title: Yes or no
notes.text: Keep the sentence as it is and raise your voice at the end.

exercises.prompt: How do you turn ყავა გინდა into a question?
options: Raise your voice at the end
exercises.explanation: Yes/no questions are the same words, asked.

notes.title: Not, can't, don't
notes.text: Put the little word right before the verb.

exercises.explanation: ნუ asks someone not to do something.

options: At the end of the sentence

notes.text: Where English puts a little word before, Georgian adds an ending.
